header.title: Papyrus "Bremner Rhind" (pBM 10188): AI translation (Claude)
header.author: Late funerary papyri
header.source: Translated by Claude (claude-opus-5-5, Anthropic) from the library's urn:egy:tla:bbawtotenlit:papyrus-bremner-rhind-pbm-10188:translit, from the Thesaurus Linguae Aegyptiae (2018), in Simon Schweitzer's AED-TEI (CC BY-SA 4.0), one English line for each line of the original. Only some passages are translated so far: those that the Atlas of Ancient Myth, Magic in the Ancient Texts and the demons-and-angels study cite.
header.statement: An AI-generated translation. No specialist has reviewed it.

notes.4.392: srḫ,y: 'accuser, opponent'. ry wꜣḏ: 'green' or 'fresh' ink. mn,w km, the material of the black cords, is unidentified (šn may be 'hair' or 'cord'). mn,t, here 'furnace', is uncertain.
notes.4.796: ṯꜣs,t, here 'bundle', is uncertain: perhaps a knot or a container. ry wꜣḏ: 'green' or 'fresh' ink.
notes.4.1232: 4.1233: jwi̯≡f-pw is the closing formula ('it has come [to its end]'). In the list, ḫr is read 'fallen'. Names whose sense is clear are translated: Terrible-of-Face (nḥꜣ-ḥr), the Roarer (hmhm,dj), Evil-of-Character (ḏw-qd), Opener-of-the-Banks (wbꜣ-jdb), the Enemy (ḫrwy), the Dark One (knm,tj), the Secret One (štꜣ), Mighty-of-Face (sḫm-ḥr), Rebellious-of-Heart (ẖꜣk-jb), the Swallower (ꜥm), the Rebel (sbj). The rest are kept as names, several in foreign-looking group writing; Khesefher (ḫsf-ḥr) may mean 'face-repeller', Sebaenseba (sbꜣ-n-sbꜣ) 'star of stars' or 'gate of gates'. ky-ḏd introduces a variant. 5.32, 5.35: mdn is unexplained, perhaps a knife or an inscribed label. 5.33: štꜣ-mdw 'secret of words', sense uncertain. 5.35: mꜣjw 'lion' or 'cat'.
notes.4.1: Wennefer is an epithet of Osiris. Ipet-sut is Karnak. 4.3: dp is read as 'taste' (of the spittle); it may stand for tp, 'your head, Apophis'.
notes.4.121: ꜣmm =f, here 'he is to be burned' (ꜣm 'burn'). m ꜥḥꜥ, 'at the standing [of the sun]', taken as noon. ꜥnḫ,t, 'the Land of Life', the west where the sun sets. psḏn,tjw, tp-ꜣbd, 6,nt and 15,nt are the festivals of the new moon, the first of the month, and the sixth and fifteenth days of the lunar month.
notes.4.124: ḫsꜣw: a plant or fuel, unidentified. ẖꜥꜥ: unidentified, perhaps a vessel. smn m [j]ḫ,t wꜥ.t, 'fixed as one thing', sense uncertain. pẖr-šw,t, 'the turning of the shadow', perhaps the afternoon. The Roarer (hmhm,tj) and Terrible-of-Face (nḥꜣw-ḥr) are names of Apophis.
notes.4.134: ⸌bjn⸍ ('bad') is written above the line. 4.135 seems to state that the rite was seen to work; the sense is uncertain.
notes.4.427: jꜣhꜣ and gm,ṱ are uncertain. Menhu (Mnḥ.w): slaughtering gods, or 'butchers'. snj, here 'sever', is uncertain. 4.430 lacks a verb or preposition; 'at' is supplied.
notes.4.474: 4.476: sꜣtꜣ is taken as 'snakes' (sꜣ-tꜣ, 'son of earth'); it could also be 'ground'. 4.477: ṯꜣs 'tie, knot'; nnw 'inertness, weariness'; the clause is obscure.
notes.4.503: 4.503 is obscure: ḏbꜣ 'replace, restore'; [s]pri̯ is taken as 'make come forth'; wꜣb.w 'roots'. 'She' is probably the Eye of the preceding lines. Horus-Khenty-en-irty (Ḥr-ḫnt,j-n-jr,tj): a form of Horus, perhaps 'foremost of the two eyes' or 'he who has no eyes'.
notes.4.521: 4.522: sb, here 'blaze', is uncertain. 4.524: mtꜣ is read both as verb and noun ('pierce', 'lance'); bjꜣ 'metal', perhaps iron. 4.525: m dm wn is obscure (dm 'sharp, pierce'). 4.526: ꜣ,t 'moment' or 'onslaught'.
notes.4.686: sḫ,ty, written twice (perhaps male and female), is unidentified; perhaps a word for adversary. ṯꜣs,t, here 'bundle', is uncertain. rdi̯.t n jr,w, 'giving to figures', sense uncertain.
notes.4.833: ḫnm 'join' or 'smell'. šꜥyd 'slaughter, cutting'. 4.836: the editor replaces the written j:q with ꜥḥꜥ ('halt').

nodes.text: Hathor has power over her father's rebels in that name of hers, Sekhmet.

Beginning of the Book of Overthrowing Apophis, the enemy of Ra, the enemy of Wennefer, may he live, prosper and be healthy, justified, made for the temple of Amun-Ra, lord of the thrones of the Two Lands, foremost of Ipet-sut, as the daily requirement of every day.
Spell for spitting on Apophis.
Words to be spoken: Taste, Apophis! Four times.
This spell is to be said over an Apophis drawn on a new sheet of papyrus in green ink, and a figure of Apophis of wax with his name marked on him in green ink, put to the fire.

He is to be burned when Ra shows himself at dawn, at noon likewise, in the evening when Ra sets in the Land of Life, at the sixth hour of the night, at the eighth hour of the day, until evening comes, and indeed every hour of the day and of the night, at the new-moon festival, by day, at the first-of-the-month festival, at the sixth-day festival and the fifteenth-day festival, likewise every day.
Overthrowing Apophis truly: it is burning [him] in a fire of *ḫsꜣw*, putting his remains into a *ẖꜥꜥ* with urine, fixed together as one mass.

You shall do the same at the sixth hour of the night and at the eighth hour of the day: putting Apophis into the fire, spitting on him many, many times at the beginning of every hour of the day until the shadow turns.
After this, at the sixth hour of the day, you shall put Apophis into the fire, spitting on him, rubbing [him] out with your left foot, repelling the Roarer and Terrible-of-Face.
It is his rescue from every bad and evil thing, truly.
I have seen [it]; it came about through me.
The first book of overthrowing Apophis, the enemy of Ra.
Words to be spoken: Fall on your face, Apophis, that enemy of Ra!
Retreat backwards, fallen one, rebel, who has no arms, who has no legs!

Now you are to make all the enemies of Ra and all the enemies of Pharaoh, may he live, prosper and be healthy, dead or living, and every accuser who is in his heart, [with] the names of their fathers, their mothers and their children, of every family, written in green ink on a new sheet of papyrus, their names marked on their breasts; made of wax likewise, bound with cords of black *mnw*; spat upon, rubbed out with the left foot, felled with spear and knife, put on the fire in the furnace(?) of the coppersmiths.
Your heart is troubled(?), your body is in grief(?);
you are cut short, there is no going forth for you;
you are assigned to those who are in the slaughterhouse, the *Menhu*, sharp of knife, that they may sever(?) your head;
they are [at] your neck;
they deal with you again and again;
they bring you down into the raging fire.
Words spoken by the Lord of All, which he said after he came into being: It is I who came into being as Khepri.
The sky had not come into being,
the earth had not come into being,
snakes and creeping things had not been created in that place.
I bound [things] together from them in Nun, in inertness;
I had not found a place where I could stand.
I replaced what she had taken in it; I made [things] come forth from her roots(?).
I created all creeping things and everything that came into being among them.
Then Shu and Tefnut bore Geb and Nut.
Then Geb and Nut bore Osiris, Horus-Khenty-en-irty, Seth, Isis and Nephthys from one womb, one after another of them.
They bore their multitudes in this land.
His bones are burned,
his limbs are in the blaze(?) of the fire.
I have commanded Horus against him,
Great-of-Strength at the prow of the bark of Ra; he has pierced him with his lance of metal.
He makes his body into something pierced(?);
he repels [him] at his onslaught(?), after he has raged;
he makes him vomit [what is] in his heart.

Now you shall write these names of every *sḫty*, every *sḫty* of whom your heart is afraid, as every enemy of Pharaoh, may he live, prosper and be healthy, dead or living, the names of their fathers, the names of their mothers, the names of their children, inside a bundle(?), giving [them] to figures of wax, and putting [them] on the fire after the name of Apophis.

Words to be spoken over an Apophis made of wax, his name written on him in green ink, and his figure on a new sheet of papyrus, and figures of every enemy of Pharaoh, may he live, prosper and be healthy, dead or living, of wax, their names written on them in green ink, bound inside a bundle(?);
spit on them, rub them out with your left foot.
The smell of the great slaughterhouse is in your flesh;
you are joined(?) to the slaughter of the great god;
Serqet enchants you, she leads you astray.
Halt, halt! You are fallen, fallen, by this magic in my mouth!
I put you into the fire, that it may destroy you.
'The Book of the Lord of All' is its name.
It is finished.
The names of Apophis, which shall not exist.
Apophis is fallen: Menshed.
Apophis is fallen: Djudju.
Apophis is fallen: Terrible-of-Face.
Apophis is fallen: the Roarer.
Apophis is fallen: Evil-of-Character.
Apophis is fallen: Qerner.
Apophis is fallen: Yubani.
Apophis is fallen: Ama.
Apophis is fallen: Opener-of-the-Banks.
Apophis is fallen: Siadjta.
Apophis is fallen: the Enemy.
Apophis is fallen: the Dark One.
Apophis is fallen: the Secret One.
Apophis is fallen: Serem.
Apophis is fallen: Mighty-of-Face.
Apophis is fallen: Wenti.
Apophis is fallen: Keriumemti.
Apophis is fallen: Khesefher.
Apophis is fallen: Sebaenseba.
Apophis is fallen: Rebellious-of-Heart.
Apophis is fallen: Khanraa; variant: Kharu.
Apophis is fallen: Nay.
Apophis is fallen: the Swallower.
Apophis is fallen: Turu[a].
Apophis is fallen: Yuba[t].
Apophis is fallen: Wai.
Apophis is fallen: Kharubu-the-Evil.
Apophis is fallen: Sau.
Apophis is fallen: the Rebel.
The drawings of the band, which are to be made on a new sheet of papyrus; they are felled and put on the fire.
Then one makes a snake with its tail in its mouth, its face downward, its *mdn* on its back, saying: 'Apophis is fallen: Betj.'
Make another: it is Secret-of-Words(?).
Make another: figures of four enemies with the face of [a snake], bound and fettered, their arms behind them; they are the Children of Revolt.
Make another: a snake with the face of a lion, its face downward, its *mdn* saying: 'the Roarer'.
